prompt.text: Use code 1 for a table, 2 for a bar graph, 3 for a pictogram, 4 for a line graph and 5 for a pie chart. A town plan divides all of its land into housing, parks, roads and shops, and the percentages add up to exactly 100%. A presentation needs the relative share of each use at a glance. For the reason code, use 1 if a bar graph cannot show percentages, 2 if a bar graph cannot show four categories, or 3 if a bar graph compares the uses but does not show them as parts of one whole. Enter a two-digit number: the first digit is the code of the most suitable display and the second digit is the reason code.

content.text: Ask whether the four land uses together make up one whole.
The four percentages add up to 100%, and the audience must see at a glance how large each share is. Choose the display that shows shares of one whole, then think about what a bar graph does not show.
A pie chart shows the four land uses as parts of one whole at a glance. A bar graph can compare the uses, but it does not show them as parts of one whole, so the reason code is 3.
